H.P. Co. Hoosah Alex, April 24, 1915 Dearest Sister: I am very glad to hear from you and glad to know that you are alright so as Minnie. And we are all right too and the baby. I am sending you the money now for your fare to come home. We would like to have you come home right away and work. I hope this money will find you right. We are sending you $48 dollars, and just soon as you come we will put you to work right away. Then we will pay more on them. Just as soon as you get this money try to take the big boat to H.P. Co. If you take the boat it only going to Juneau you won't have the money enough to use and you will have a hard time. So we want you to let the subj help you to find out what boat is coming over here. Just as soon as this Cannery closed we will bring you right back to Selma with us. We going back to Minneapolis this year. This Cannery will closed about September. So we want you to come soon. as the School closed. And make enough money for yourself to use it in School. We would like to have the Dept help you on The Way come home. Henry don't have time to write him a letter so he never write to him. He is busy all the time. There are Women here making Cans, some girls are working now. You will get the job just as soon as you come. I will take care of you. You will stay with me. Your Mother is very sick Julia. The Doctor said she won't get well. But the rest of the family is all right. Don't forget to take the steam boat as coming over here. The School don't closed on June. Every School closes on May. So when you get this money in time. Try and come just as soon as you can. See I just feel awful tired this afternoon. The baby kept me busy all the time. And keeping house clean up and wash and cook baking bread and the baby cries all the time. Makes me feel tired. We are going to have a dance tonight and I'm ready to go and leave the baby home with her papa. Boiv is everything going on in school. I hope you girls enjoying yourself and doing fine with your school work. I am writing this letter while the baby is sleeping so I have much to say. I just got your letter this afternoon and started to answer it. Eugene Fennell is a big fellow now, you would tell who he is when you come. Father has a baby girl both again this year. Kate Brown is a big girl now. I don't know yet the new baby's name. There are not here, they are gone to P.A.F.E.D. and Lucy Brown. Archie Helssinger was in here last night. He came in to see the baby and said hello to you. I think I have to close now as I have no more news to tell you. I will be looking for you every big boat comes in. Maryjette may send you her best love. From yours truly sister Miss J. May Moy. Miss Elise Bowen. Cushman Greacle School. Tacoma Wash. CASE RECORD. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parents are living or dead, this fact must be given. The person who signs the blank as consenter to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of kin," leaving unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. Compliance must be given to all orders and instructions which have been promulgated in connection with the new course of study issued December 1, 1915. The information as to public school facilities called for in the certificate of the Superintendent (third page hereof) must be given, and all superintendents are especially directed to exhaust every means to secure enrollment of Indian children in the State public schools, pursuant to instructions heretofore issued in this regard. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., July 28, 1919 Mrs. Henry Moy Hoonah, Alaska Dear Mrs. Moy: Your letter to Elsie passed through my hands. Elsie has been a very good girl indeed this year and I believe it would be better for her to stay since the vacation is more than half over. School begins September 2nd and she would be very late returning if she did not insist on staying home altogether. You know she might run around too much and get out of the notion to continue her education. I don't know when I could get passage for Elsie as I had to wait from July 12 to the 29th before I could get passage for Minnie Knudsen. It is too late now to think of going home and would only waste good money for a very short vacation. Sincerely yours, Superintendent. EHH:MG Enc. Money Order #8905-$60.00. Hoonah Alaska H. Pby Co. July 8, 1919. Dear Sister: I am going to answer your letter and was very glad to hear from you. And sorry to hear you are alone there. You know how you was last summer so we didn't dare to send you some money for you fair to come home but I hope you will be alright this time. And promise to be a good girl. And you said you were a good girl in School. And I hope you will be the same when or come home too. You know your mother is dead. You don't want to be sorry now. Be good and try to learn all you can for your own good. We was not going to send you some for you finar. But this time there no body to stay with your grandmother and no body to take care of her. So we write for you to come home and take care of her for this summer and we will send you back again when the season is over. We are sending you $20 that will be enough. Your grandmother is 93 & mine 92, that makes $40 all together. Come right over when you get this money. If there won't let you come over send the money back. Hope to see you some alright. I got another more baby girl. Maritza is a big girl now running around and there alright. From your sister Mrs Henry Moy Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., June 14, 1919 Mr. Henry Moys Hoonah Packing Co. Hoonah, Alaska My dear Mr. Moys: Elsie Brown has referred your letter to me in which you request that Elsie Brown give you a Power of Attorney in favor of Elsie's sister May, authorizing her to act for Elsie in the probating of Aunt Julia Reese's estate. Inasmuch as Elsie is only Seventeen years of age, she does not possess the legal right to give power of attorney for any one to represent her but her Guardian does possess the right. In no case can a minor interests be disposed of without an order from the Court. To protect the minors interests still more, the Law allows her a reasonable time after she reaches legal age to take action for redress in case of any wrong or injury to interests having been made during her minority. If you apply to the Court for guardianship papers over your sister-in-law, the Court will undoubtedly approve your request. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MC Miss C. Brown Cushman School Tacoma Wash. 212-10 Ave South St Seattle Wash. Oct 14/8 Miss E. Brown Dearest Sweetheart: I receive your sweet letter and am very glad to get it. As you say that you always think of me, for my part I am always thinking of you. For only part I am alone. Some for you baby baby I can tell how much I love you nothing in my heart but you little baby. I can't sleep I can eat in amount of think of you sweetheart I always dream of you my baby. But dear I don't believe that you got love about me I know that she's more dearest than here in Tacoma. I see you that you was going while the Native (man) in the street of Tacoma; you don't see me on that time. I was standing in the corner of St on that time. So from that time my heart was crying about our promise. So from now till me the truth tell me half love of your heart about me weather you tell me true. I can tell myself about you. I don't know wants get a true love about you. I know another is so many boys sweetheart of yours in this world not only one till then is some that you never tell me. So please nothing in may remain but you it can't tell on this world. I think I'll close my best true and kisses to you I hope you always good and remember me all the time, before and not to forget to sent you both pictures and Mancine. Good Night Sweet Kisses Yours Coby B. P. Alohim Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington June 29, 1918. Miss Elsie Brown Hoonah, Alaska Dear Miss Elsie: I am sending herewith your two war saving Certificates. I hope you will save every cent possible and will invest in other stamps until your card is full. It will be a good paying investment and will show that you are a real patriot, willing to do your share in helping to win this war. Don't be a slacker. Save and invest your money in war saving stamps. Hoping you will have a fine vacation and will bring dozens of new pupils back with you, I am Very sincerely yours, Superintendent Enrolled Oct. 22, 1917 5-192a BRIEF.
